newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Suharto warns rich to help the poor.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Suharto warns rich to help the poor.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto threatened on Friday to force the rich to help the poor if they did not do so voluntarily.

In 1995, Suharto appealed to private companies and individuals with an annual after-tax income of more than 100 million rupiah ($43,140) to donate two percent of their earnings to a poverty relief foundation he chairs.

"If the appeal is ignored, we can make rules to enforce it. This means there is an obligation for the rich to help the poor," the president said at a meeting with university graduates. "This does not go against the constitution."
In his latest call, Suharto said only half the country's 11,000 high-bracket taxpayers had contributed to poverty relief.
The government estimates about 26 millon people out of a population of nearly 200 million live below the poverty line.
The programme aims to provide funds for small-scale business activities and other assistance schemes.
